newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU starts formal probe into Creditanstalt buy.
newsitem.headline: EU starts formal probe into Creditanstalt buy.

text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday it had received formal notification of the proposed acquisition of Austrian bank Creditanstalt-Bankverein by rival Bank Austria AG.
The Commission has been investigating the controversial privatisation of Creditanstalt since early December due to fears that the deal may harm competition particularly on the Austrian market.
The 17.2 billion schilling sale brings together Austria's two largest banks.

But the Commission's fears also arise from the fact that Bank Austria itself is indirectly controlled by the City of Vienna, which provides an unlimited guarantee for its liabilities. This could amount to disguised subsidies as it enables Austria to compete with commercial banks for cheaper credit.

The Commission said in a statement to be published in the EU's Official Journal that Bank Austria's acquisition of Creditanstalt was submitted for clearance on February 10 under the bloc's merger rules which ban creation or strengthening of dominant positions.
It has one month from that date to clear it or start a four-month in-depth investigation.
Bank Austria was awarded the state's 70-percent voting stake in the flagship bank in January after a bitter fight which deeply divided the Social Democrat-conservative government coalition.
The subsidy probe will be separated from the merger investigation.
Austria's new finance minister Rudolf Edlinger, formerly Vienna City finance chief, is to head the discussions with the Commission.
